title: Cautionary Tales of the Sydney Opera House

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: The Sydney Opera House is one of the most iconic and distinctive buildings in the world.
sentences.zh: 悉尼歌剧院是世界上最具标志性和独特性的建筑之一。

sentences.en: It took a relative newcomer and architectural outsider to dream it up.
sentences.zh: 构想出它的是一位相对的新人和建筑界的局外人。

sentences.en: But the saga of making this future world heritage landmark a reality is a tale for the ages.
sentences.zh: 但将这座未来的世界文化遗产地标变为现实的传奇历程，堪称流芳百世。

sentences.en: A cautionary tale.
sentences.zh: 一个充满警示的传奇。

sentences.en: And for cautionary tales, I turn to the brilliant Tim Harford.
sentences.zh: 至于带有警示意味的故事，我找到了才华横溢的蒂姆·哈福德。

sentences.en: I've been dying to hear the story of the Sydney Opera House told in this way,
sentences.zh: 我一直渴望听到以这种方式讲述的悉尼歌剧院的故事，

sentences.en: and Tim and his team just nailed it.
sentences.zh: 而蒂姆和他的团队堪称完美呈现。

sentences.en: And I know you're going to love it as much as I do.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们也会和我一样喜欢它。

sentences.en: Enjoy.
sentences.zh: 请欣赏。

sentences.en: In a clearing in a forest,
sentences.zh: 在森林的一处空地上，

sentences.en: a day's walk north of Copenhagen,
sentences.zh: 向北步行一天，

sentences.en: stood a little house.
sentences.zh: 矗立着一座小房子。

sentences.en: A fairytale setting,
sentences.zh: 童话般的场景，

sentences.en: worthy of Hans Christian Andersen, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 或许配得上汉斯·克里斯蒂安·安徒生。
zh_words: 汉斯·克里斯蒂安·安徒生

sentences.en: But this is no fairytale,
sentences.zh: 但这并非童话，

sentences.en: and it wasn't a fairytale house.
sentences.zh: 它也不是什么童话里的房子。

sentences.en: It was low, flat, and minimaliSt.
sentences.zh: 它低矮、平坦且极简。

sentences.en: Denmark's first open-plan house.
sentences.zh: 丹麦第一座开放式布局的房子。

sentences.en: It had been built in 1952, without proper floor plans.
sentences.zh: 它建于1952年，没有正式的平面图。

sentences.en: The house's young architect was building his own home,
sentences.zh: 这座房子的年轻建筑师在建造自己的家，

sentences.en: and he'd insisted instead on personally directing the work as it progressed.
sentences.zh: 他坚持亲自在施工现场指挥工程的推进。

sentences.en: But it was brilliant.
sentences.zh: 但它太出色了。

sentences.en: Denmark's most celebrated architect visited the construction site
sentences.zh: 丹麦最著名的建筑师参观了施工现场，

sentences.en: and muttered under his breath,
sentences.zh: 低声嘟囔着：

sentences.en: Hell, he's better than I am.
sentences.zh: 见鬼，他比我还要厉害。

sentences.en: Maybe so.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: It was hard to be sure.
sentences.zh: 很难确定。

sentences.en: The young architect, Jorn Utzon, had won plenty of competitions,
sentences.zh: 年轻的建筑师约恩·乌松赢过很多比赛，

sentences.en: but with his career interrupted by the war,
sentences.zh: 但由于战争中断了他的职业生涯，

sentences.en: that house was almost the only thing he'd actually built.
sentences.zh: 那座房子几乎是他实际建造的唯一作品。

sentences.en: Late in January 1957, the phone in the Utzon home rang.
sentences.zh: 1957年1月末，乌松家里的电话铃响了。

sentences.en: Jorn and his wife were taking a winter walk in the woods.
sentences.zh: 约恩和妻子正在树林里进行冬日散步。

sentences.en: Their 10-year-old daughter, Lynne, was at home babysitting her newborn brother.
sentences.zh: 他们10岁的女儿琳恩在家照顾刚出生的弟弟。

sentences.en: She answered the phone.
sentences.zh: 她接了电话。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: The village operator was on the other end.
sentences.zh: 村里的接线员在电话那头。

sentences.en: She knew the family.
sentences.zh: 她认识这家人。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Is your mother home?
sentences.zh: 你妈妈在家吗？

sentences.en: No, they're out walking.
sentences.zh: 不在，他们出去散步了。

sentences.en: Quick, go find your father.
sentences.zh: 快，去找你父亲。

sentences.en: He's from the newspaper in Sydney, Australia.
sentences.zh: 他是来自澳大利亚悉尼的报社记者。

sentences.en: Lynn drops the phone, leaves her sleeping brother and grabs her bike.
sentences.zh: 琳恩扔下电话，撇下正在睡觉的弟弟，抓起她的自行车。

sentences.en: She races out into the Danish winter, yelling for her parents.
sentences.zh: 她冲进丹麦的冬日里，大声呼喊着父母。

sentences.en: It must have been alarm to see their little blonde babysitting daughter
sentences.zh: 看到他们金发的小保姆女儿

sentences.en: cycling towards them, screaming at the top of her voice.
sentences.zh: 骑着车朝他们冲过来，扯着嗓子尖叫，一定把他们吓了一跳。

sentences.en: Sydney!
sentences.zh: 悉尼！

sentences.en: Sydney!
sentences.zh: 悉尼！

sentences.en: She skids to a halt.
sentences.zh: 她一个急刹车停了下来。

sentences.en: You've won a prize.
sentences.zh: 你得奖了。

sentences.en: You've won something in Sydney.
sentences.zh: 你在悉尼中奖了。

sentences.en: Someone's on the phone and they want to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 有人在电话那头，他们想跟你说话。

sentences.en: It must have felt like a phone call from the moon.
sentences.zh: 这感觉一定像是接到了来自月球的电话。

sentences.en: The unknown young Dane, Jorn Utzon,
sentences.zh: 这位名不见经传的年轻丹麦人约恩·乌松，

sentences.en: had won an international competition to design the Sydney Opera House.
sentences.zh: 赢得了一项设计悉尼歌剧院的国际比赛。

sentences.en: But Utzon couldn't have imagined what a bitter victory it would prove to be.
sentences.zh: 但乌松当时绝不会想到，这会是一场多么苦涩的胜利。

sentences.en: I'm Tim Harford, and you're listening to Cautionary Tales.
sentences.zh: 我是蒂姆·哈福德，你收听的是《警示故事》。

sentences.en: Eugene Goossens was a distinguished violinist and conductor.
sentences.zh: 尤金·古森斯是一位杰出的小提琴家和指挥家。

sentences.en: In the 1940s, he moved from Britain to the faraway city of Sydney,
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代，他从英国搬到了遥远的悉尼市，

sentences.en: where he was struck by three things.
sentences.zh: 在那里他被三件事所震撼：

sentences.en: – the beauty of the harbour, the apparent indifference of the locals to that beauty,
sentences.zh: 港口的美景、当地人对这种美景的冷漠，

sentences.en: and the lack of a really good venue for classical music.
sentences.zh: 以及缺乏一个真正适合古典音乐的优质场馆。

sentences.en: Goossens dreamed up an idea – build a huge opera house on Bennelong Point, a finger of
sentences.zh: 古森斯萌生了一个想法——在本尼朗岬角建造一座巨大的歌剧院，这是一条

sentences.en: rock poking out into Sydney's glorious harbour, in which blue water is surrounded on all sides
sentences.zh: 伸入悉尼壮丽港口的岩石岬角，港湾碧水环绕，四周被

sentences.en: by the city and spanned by the vast arch of the Sydney Harbour Bridge.
sentences.zh: 城市环抱，还有宏伟的悉尼海港大桥横跨其上。

sentences.en: Goossens was charismatic
sentences.zh: 古森斯极具个人魅力，

sentences.en: and local politicians were keen to show that they could deliver cultural amenities for Sydney
sentences.zh: 当地政客也急于向悉尼选民证明他们能够兑现

sentences.en: voters.
sentences.zh: 文化设施的承诺。

sentences.en: They formed a committee which announced an open competition to design the new opera house.
sentences.zh: 他们组建了一个委员会，宣布了一项设计新歌剧院的公开比赛。

sentences.en: Anyone, even an unknown young architect from Denmark, could try to win.
sentences.zh: 任何人，甚至是一个来自丹麦的不知名年轻建筑师，都可以尝试赢得比赛。

sentences.en: As Goossens' grand
sentences.zh: 正当古森斯的宏伟

sentences.en: project gathered momentum, he flew back to London to be knighted by the Queen.
sentences.zh: 项目如火如荼地推进时，他飞回伦敦接受女王的册封。

sentences.en: And on his return,
sentences.zh: 而在他返回时，

sentences.en: tipped off by a journalist, customs officers asked to search his luggage.
sentences.zh: 由于记者的通风报信，海关官员要求搜查他的行李。

sentences.en: They found it to be packed
sentences.zh: 他们发现里面塞满了

sentences.en: with naughty photographs and even naughtier rubber masks.
sentences.zh: 不雅照片，甚至还有更加不堪的橡胶面具。

sentences.en: In 1950s Australia, it was a scandal.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代的澳大利亚，这是一桩丑闻。

sentences.en: Sir Eugene fled back to London, a broken man.
sentences.zh: 尤金爵士仓皇逃回伦敦，成了一个心碎的废人。

sentences.en: Alas, Sir Eugene's fate – great talent, self-inflicted wounds and a tragic end to a great career – is just the overture to the story of the Sydney Opera House,
sentences.zh: 可惜的是，尤金爵士的命运——卓越的天赋、作茧自缚的伤痕以及辉煌职业生涯的悲惨结局——仅仅是悉尼歌剧院故事的序曲，

sentences.en: in which the same dramatic beats would play out on a much bigger stage.
sentences.zh: 在这个更大的舞台上，同样的戏剧性节奏将再次上演。

sentences.en: Not that anyone should have expected the Sydney Opera House to be an easy project.
sentences.zh: 并不是说任何人会指望悉尼歌剧院会是一个轻松的项目。

sentences.en: Sir Eugene had wanted big concert halls,
sentences.zh: 尤金爵士想要大型音乐厅，

sentences.en: but Benelong Point was a cramped site.
sentences.zh: 但本尼朗岬角是一个狭窄的地块。

sentences.en: The premier of the state wanted a grand legacy,
sentences.zh: 州长想要一份宏大的遗产，

sentences.en: a building for the ages,
sentences.zh: 一座流芳百世的建筑，

sentences.en: but no politician wanted to raise taxes to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 但没有哪个政客愿意通过加税来为之买单。

sentences.en: And opera houses are actually rather ungainly structures.
sentences.zh: 而且歌剧院实际上相当笨拙。

sentences.en: Their bulging towers for stage machinery
sentences.zh: 它们用于舞台机械的凸起塔楼

sentences.en: are usually hidden behind grand facades.
sentences.zh: 通常隐藏在宏伟的外墙后面。

sentences.en: But Sydney's Opera House couldn't hide.
sentences.zh: 但悉尼歌剧院无处可藏。

sentences.en: It would be visible across the water, from north, east and west,
sentences.zh: 它从水面上清晰可见，从北、东、西三个方向，

sentences.en: even from above, from the monumental Sydney Harbour Bridge.
sentences.zh: 甚至从上方、从宏伟的悉尼海港大桥上也能看到。

sentences.en: In announcing their competition then,
sentences.zh: 因此，在宣布比赛时，

sentences.en: the committee laid down the challenge to architects from around the world.
sentences.zh: 委员会向全世界的建筑师发起了挑战。

sentences.en: Design an opera house for us.
sentences.zh: 为我们设计一座歌剧院。

sentences.en: It needs to be huge, fit onto a tiny site,
sentences.zh: 它必须体量巨大，建在狭小的地块上，

sentences.en: look amazing from any angle and be cheap.
sentences.zh: 从任何角度看都要惊艳，而且还得便宜。

sentences.en: Knock yourselves out.
sentences.zh: 尽管大显身手吧。

sentences.en: In January 1957, the time came to choose a winner.
sentences.zh: 1957年1月，选择赢家的时候到了。

sentences.en: The judging panel spent four days sifting through more than 200 entries and drawing up a shortliSt.
sentences.zh: 评审团花了四天时间从200多份参赛作品中筛选并拟定了一份入围名单。

sentences.en: They were waiting for the arrival of the final judge, an architectural rock star,
sentences.zh: 他们在等待最后一位评委的到来，那是一位建筑界的摇滚巨星，

sentences.en: the great Finnish-American architect Eero Saarinen.
sentences.zh: 伟大的芬兰裔美国建筑师埃罗·萨里宁。

sentences.en: But he was running late.
sentences.zh: 但他迟到了。

sentences.en: That was understandable.
sentences.zh: 这可以理解。

sentences.en: Saarinen was a busy man, designer of landmarks
sentences.zh: 萨里宁是个大忙人，他是许多地标建筑的设计师，

sentences.en: such as the celebrated TWA terminal at New York's International Airport.
sentences.zh: 比如纽约国际机场著名的环球航空公司航站楼。

sentences.en: And if buildings like that helped New York to feel like the centre of the world,
sentences.zh: 如果这样的建筑能让纽约感到自己是世界的中心，

sentences.en: then Sydney, at the world's edge, wanted some of that starduSt.
sentences.zh: 那么位于世界边缘的悉尼，也渴望沾染一点这种明星光环。

sentences.en: When the other judges showed Eero Saarinen the ten leading entries,
sentences.zh: 当其他评委向埃罗·萨里宁展示了十个领先的参赛作品时，

sentences.en: everyone could tell that he wasn't impressed.
sentences.zh: 所有人都能看出他并不为之所动。

sentences.en: The ideas were awkward compromises,
sentences.zh: 这些构想都是尴尬的妥协，

sentences.en: predictably boxed in by their attempts to satisfy
sentences.zh: 不出意料地被那些试图满足比赛中

sentences.en: the contradictory requirements of the competition.
sentences.zh: 相互矛盾的要求的想法所局限。

sentences.en: Saarinen shook his head and went for a stroll to Bennelong Point.
sentences.zh: 萨里宁摇了摇头，去本尼朗岬角散步了。

sentences.en: He sat and sketched for a while.
sentences.zh: 他坐下来画了一会儿草图。

sentences.en: Caressed on three sides by the lapping waters of Sydney Harbour,
sentences.zh: 三面被悉尼港起伏的波涛轻抚，

sentences.en: it really was a magnificent spot.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个绝佳的地点。

sentences.en: He returned to the judging room
sentences.zh: 他回到评审室，

sentences.en: and started flipping through the rejects.
sentences.zh: 开始翻阅那些被淘汰的作品。

sentences.en: There was one which stood out as completely different,
sentences.zh: 有一个作品显得截然不同，

sentences.en: even though it was really little more than a sketch.
sentences.zh: 尽管它其实不过是一张草图。

sentences.en: There was a monumental base reminiscent of an Aztec pyramid
sentences.zh: 那里有一个让人联想到阿兹特克金字塔

sentences.en: or a Chinese imperial palace.
sentences.zh: 或中国皇家宫殿的宏伟基座。

sentences.en: Floating above it were light, shell-like roof structures
sentences.zh: 悬浮在其上方的是轻盈、贝壳状的屋顶结构，

sentences.en: overlapping like the sails of some grand ship.
sentences.zh: 像某艘大船的船帆一样层层重叠。

sentences.en: It was like no building Saarinen had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 这是萨里宁从未见过的建筑。

sentences.en: He laid it out, stepped back to ponder it,
sentences.zh: 他把它摊开，退后一步沉思，

sentences.en: stepped forward to peer at the details.
sentences.zh: 又上前一步仔细端详细节。

sentences.en: Then he turned to the other judges.
sentences.zh: 然后他转向其他评委。

sentences.en: Gentlemen, here is your opera house.
sentences.zh: 先生们，这就是你们的歌剧院。

sentences.en: Twelve days later, the state premier, Joseph Cahill,
sentences.zh: 十二天后，州长约瑟夫·卡希尔

sentences.en: stands in front of the cameras with a sealed envelope.
sentences.zh: 拿着一个密封的信封站在镜头前。

sentences.en: He's a former trade union organiser,
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名工会组织者，

sentences.en: not your stereotypical opera-goer,
sentences.zh: 不是那种典型的歌剧观众，

sentences.en: But now that the disgraced Sir Eugene Goossens has fled the country,
sentences.zh: 但现在名誉扫地的尤金·古森斯爵士已经逃离了这个国家，

sentences.en: Cahill has surprised some people by stepping up as the Opera House's biggest champion.
sentences.zh: 卡希尔挺身而出，成为歌剧院最坚定的捍卫者，这让一些人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Like any good politician, he's going to milk this dramatic moment.
sentences.zh: 像任何优秀的政客一样，他要充分利用这个戏剧性的时刻。

sentences.en: The winning design, he announces, is scheme number 218.
sentences.zh: 他宣布，获胜的设计方案是218号方案。

sentences.en: And who designed that?
sentences.zh: 那是谁设计的？

sentences.en: Cahill doesn't have the name to hand.
sentences.zh: 卡希尔手头没有这个名字。

sentences.en: An official hurries forward, rummages in the envelope, pulls out a second document.
sentences.zh: 一位官员匆忙上前，在信封里翻找，抽出了第二份文件。

sentences.en: Ah yes, a scheme number 218, submitted by, um, Jorn Utzen of Hellebeek, Denmark.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，218号方案，由……嗯，来自丹麦赫尔辛厄的约恩·乌松提交。

sentences.en: Jorn Utzen?
sentences.zh: 约恩·乌松？

sentences.en: Who?
sentences.zh: 谁？

sentences.en: A reporter from the Sydney Morning Herald places a long-distance call to directory assistants in Hellebeek.
sentences.zh: 《悉尼先驱晨报》的一名记者给赫尔辛厄的查号台打了个长途电话。

sentences.en: They try Utzon's office number.
sentences.zh: 他们试了乌松办公室的电话号码。

sentences.en: He's not there.
sentences.zh: 他不在。

sentences.en: Then they try his home number.
sentences.zh: 然后他们又试了他家的号码。

sentences.en: The operator comes back on the line.
sentences.zh: 接线员重新上线。

sentences.en: Apparently, he's gone out for a walk,
sentences.zh: 显然，他出去散步了，

sentences.en: but his daughter has gone to find him.
sentences.zh: 但他女儿去找他了。

sentences.en: Is it OK to hold?
sentences.zh: 可以稍等吗？

sentences.en: For the first interview with the unknown winner
sentences.zh: 对于悉尼歌剧院设计比赛

sentences.en: of the Sydney Opera House competition?
sentences.zh: 这位名不见经传的获胜者的首次采访？

sentences.en: Sure, he'll hold.
sentences.zh: 当然，他会等的。

sentences.en: All of Australia wants to know about the mysterious Yawn Utzon.
sentences.zh: 全澳大利亚都想了解这位神秘的“约恩·乌松”。

sentences.en: When the winning sketch was published, public opinion was divided.
sentences.zh: 当获胜的草图公布时，公众舆论意见不一。

sentences.en: Letters published in the Sydney Morning Herald described the design as
sentences.zh: 《悉尼先驱晨报》上发表的读者来信将该设计描述为

sentences.en: a wonderful piece of sculpture, a haystack covered by several tarpaulins,
sentences.zh: 一块精彩的雕塑、一堆盖着几块防水布的干草垛、

sentences.en: a ray of hope, a sink with plates stacked in readiness for washing,
sentences.zh: 一缕希望之光、一个堆满待洗盘子的水槽、

sentences.en: some large lovely ship of the imagination,
sentences.zh: 某种想象中宏大可爱的巨轮、

sentences.en: a hideous parachute which we cannot fold up and put away.
sentences.zh: 一个我们无法折叠收纳的丑陋降落伞。

sentences.en: But when Jorn Utzon arrived in Sydney, some of those doubts began to melt away.
sentences.zh: 但当约恩·乌松抵达悉尼时，其中一些疑虑开始消散。

sentences.en: Tall, blonde, blue-eyed, that sexy Danish accent, movie star looks.
sentences.zh: 高大、金发、蓝眼睛、性感的丹麦口音、电影明星般的长相。

sentences.en: He's our Gary Cooper, declared one local lady.
sentences.zh: “他是我们的加里·库珀，”一位当地女士宣称。

sentences.en: Sydney was a bustling place, but it usually felt far from the world's spotlight.
sentences.zh: 悉尼是一个繁华的地方，但它通常感觉远离世界聚光灯。

sentences.en: Now, it felt as though Hollywood had come to call.
sentences.zh: 现在，感觉就像好莱坞来访了一般。

sentences.en: The city fell in love with a man.
sentences.zh: 这座城市爱上了一个男人。

sentences.en: Professional architects were more cautious.
sentences.zh: 专业建筑师则更为谨慎。

sentences.en: The sketches were impressive, sure,
sentences.zh: 草图确实令人印象深刻，

sentences.en: but Utzon hadn't submitted all the plans and drawings the competition rules specified.
sentences.zh: 但乌松并没有提交比赛规则指定的所有计划和图纸。

sentences.en: One Australian art critic described his entry as
sentences.zh: 一位澳大利亚艺术评论家将他的参赛作品形容为

sentences.en: nothing more than a magnificent doodle.
sentences.zh: 不过是一幅宏大的涂鸦。

sentences.en: What's more, Utzon's doodled building overstepped the site's boundaries.
sentences.zh: 更何况，乌松涂鸦式的建筑超出了场地的边界。

sentences.en: Then there was the question of whether its glorious sail-like roof structures
sentences.zh: 然后问题来了：其辉煌的帆状屋顶结构

sentences.en: could actually stand up.
sentences.zh: 究竟能不能立得住。

sentences.en: None of this worried Eero Saarinen,
sentences.zh: 这一切都没有困扰埃罗·沙里宁，

sentences.en: the rock star architect who'd pushed his fellow judges
sentences.zh: 这位极力促使其他评委

sentences.en: into choosing Utzon's entry.
sentences.zh: 选择乌松作品的明星建筑师。

sentences.en: Nothing to it, said Saarinen about those roof structures.
sentences.zh: “这没什么难的，”沙里宁谈到那些屋顶结构时说。

sentences.en: Three inches thick at the top and, say, 12 inches thick at the base.
sentences.zh: 顶部厚三英寸，底部大概厚十二英寸。

sentences.en: But concrete shell architecture was still an emerging field
sentences.zh: 但混凝土壳体建筑当时仍是一个新兴领域，

sentences.en: and many experts weren't so sure.
sentences.zh: 许多专家并不那么确信。

sentences.en: Yes, eggshell structures could be surprisingly strong,
sentences.zh: 是的，蛋壳结构可以出奇地坚固，

sentences.en: but cut the egg in half and much of that strength is gone.
sentences.zh: 但把鸡蛋切成两半，大部分强度就消失了。

sentences.en: And Utzon's opera house roof?
sentences.zh: 而乌松的歌剧院屋顶呢？

sentences.en: It was a series of quarter shells.
sentences.zh: 它是一系列四分之一的壳体。

sentences.en: Until this point, Utzon had taken no engineering advice.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，乌松没有咨询过任何工程意见。

sentences.en: And he wouldn't have long to figure out a solution,
sentences.zh: 而且他没有多少时间来想出解决方案，

sentences.en: because the project's champion, State Premier Joseph Cahill,
sentences.zh: 因为该项目标兵、州长约瑟夫·卡希尔

sentences.en: was a man in a hurry.
sentences.zh: 是一个急性子的人。

sentences.en: He was a heavy smoker with a history of health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他是个老烟民，有健康问题病史。

sentences.en: He knew he was also at risk of losing the next election.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己也面临着输掉下次选举的风险。

sentences.en: He wanted a monument to his place in history.
sentences.zh: 他想要一座奠定他在历史地位的纪念碑。

sentences.en: So he instructed the Opera House team.
sentences.zh: 于是他向歌剧院团队下达了指示。

sentences.en: Go down to Bennelong Point and make such progress
sentences.zh: 去本尼朗角大举推进工程，

sentences.en: that no one who succeeds me can stop this going through to completion.
sentences.zh: 让任何继任者都无法阻止这个项目顺利竣工。

sentences.en: As a result, the building started
sentences.zh: 结果，在乌松弄清结构基础之前，

sentences.en: before Utzon could figure out the structural basics.
sentences.zh: 建筑工程就已经开始了。

sentences.en: Joseph Cahill laid the foundation stone on 2 March 1959.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·卡希尔于1959年3月2日奠基。

sentences.en: Within a year, he was dead, killed by his third heart attack.
sentences.zh: 不到一年他就去世了，死于他的第三次心脏病发作。

sentences.en: But just as he'd intended, so much work had already been done
sentences.zh: 但正如他所愿，大量工作已经完成，

sentences.en: that stopping the project was unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 以至于想要叫停项目是不可想象的。

sentences.en: By now, an engineer had been found.
sentences.zh: 此时，人们已经找到了一位工程师。

sentences.en: His name was Ove Arup, the Anglo-Danish boss of Ove Arup & Partners, a respected engineering firm.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫奥维·阿鲁普，是备受尊敬的工程公司奥维·阿鲁普合伙人的英籍丹麦老板。

sentences.en: The two Danes, Utzon and Arup, had been working together to try to figure out a solution to the structural problem.
sentences.zh: 两位丹麦人乌松和阿鲁普一直在合作，试图找出结构问题的解决方案。

sentences.en: And it was at this point that Arup informed Utzon of the bad news.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，阿鲁普向乌松通报了一个坏消息。

sentences.en: His beautiful, freestanding roof shells simply couldn't be built.
sentences.zh: 他那些美丽、独立的屋顶壳体根本无法建造。

sentences.en: There's no such thing as too many Danes.
sentences.zh: 丹麦人永远不嫌多。

sentences.en: So let's meet a third, Bent Flubia.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们见识第三个，本特·弗卢比亚。

sentences.en: He's the world's leading expert on large projects
sentences.zh: 他是大型项目领域的全球顶尖专家，

sentences.en: and on why these megaprojects are so often delivered late and way over budget.
sentences.zh: 专门研究为什么这些巨型项目经常延期且严重超支。

sentences.en: And he's fascinated by the Sydney Opera House
sentences.zh: 他迷恋悉尼歌剧院，

sentences.en: because it's the ultimate case study,
sentences.zh: 因为它是终极案例研究，

sentences.en: the definitive fiasco of how not to run a megaproject.
sentences.zh: 是关于如何搞砸一个巨型项目的教科书式惨败。

sentences.en: Flubier says that the original sin of many megaprojects is this.
sentences.zh: 弗卢比尔表示，许多巨型项目的原罪在于此。

sentences.en: People start building before they've figured out what they're really trying to do.
sentences.zh: 人们在还没弄清楚自己到底想做什么之前就开始建设了。

sentences.en: The ideal megaproject starts with the question, why are we doing this?
sentences.zh: 理想的巨型项目始于这样一个问题：我们为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: Then there's a long, careful planning process.
sentences.zh: 然后是一个漫长、仔细的规划过程。

sentences.en: Every detail is finalised.
sentences.zh: 每一个细节都敲定。

sentences.en: Then the expensive construction phase can be kept as short as possible, with no costly changes.
sentences.zh: 接着昂贵的施工阶段可以尽可能缩短，没有任何代价高昂的变更。

sentences.en: The Opera House violated these principles in the most flagrant way imaginable.
sentences.zh: 歌剧院以你能想象到的最公然的方式违背了这些原则。

sentences.en: Nobody ever really answered the question, why?
sentences.zh: 从来没有人真正回答过“为什么”这个问题。

sentences.en: Sir Eugene Goossens had wanted to accommodate a lot of opera goers and use the beautiful location of Bennelong Point.
sentences.zh: 尤金·古森斯爵士希望容纳大量歌剧观众并利用本尼朗角的美丽位置。

sentences.en: The state's premier, Joseph Cahill, had wanted a lasting monument on the cheap, without spending taxpayer money.
sentences.zh: 州长约瑟夫·卡希尔希望以低成本留下一个持久的纪念碑，而不花纳税人的钱。

sentences.en: Jorn Utzon wanted to build something beautiful and new.
sentences.zh: 约恩·乌松想要建造一些美丽而崭新的东西。

sentences.en: But what if you couldn't make it both beautiful and cheap?
sentences.zh: 但如果你无法做到既美观又便宜呢？

sentences.en: What if you couldn't make it big while also squeezing it onto Benelong Point?
sentences.zh: 如果你既想把它做大，又要把挤进本尼朗角呢？

sentences.en: The trade-offs were swept under the carpet.
sentences.zh: 这些权衡取舍都被掩盖了。

sentences.en: The difficult decisions postponed or ignored.
sentences.zh: 艰难的决定被推迟或忽视。

sentences.en: Then, of course, the building was rushed,
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，建筑工程被赶工了，

sentences.en: with workers digging foundations before Utzon and Arup had figured out how to build the thing.
sentences.zh: 工人在乌松和阿鲁普弄清楚如何建造它之前就开始挖掘地基了。

sentences.en: Utzon was in an impossible position.
sentences.zh: 乌松处于一个不可能的境地。

sentences.en: And Utzon wasn't blameless either.
sentences.zh: 而且乌松也不是毫无过错的。

sentences.en: Remember how he'd never
sentences.zh: 还记得他从来没有

sentences.en: drawn proper plans for his beautiful home in the Danish forest, but instead had been on site
sentences.zh: 为他在丹麦森林里美丽的家绘制过正式的图纸，而是一直在现场

sentences.en: throughout, personally directing the builders?
sentences.zh: 亲自指导建筑工人吗？

sentences.en: Careful planning was all very well, but he loved
sentences.zh: 仔细的规划固然很好，但他喜欢

sentences.en: to experiment, to feel his way through a project.
sentences.zh: 尝试，在项目中摸索前行。

sentences.en: It worked for his beautiful home,
sentences.zh: 这对他美丽的家很有效，

sentences.en: but could it also work for a colossal, structurally innovative megaproject?
sentences.zh: 但它也能适用于一个庞大且结构创新的巨型项目吗？

sentences.en: Utzon worked like an artist, not a project manager.
sentences.zh: 乌松的工作方式像个艺术家，而不是项目经理。

sentences.en: He wanted to make the final decision
sentences.zh: 他想对每一个细节做出最后决定，

sentences.en: on every detail, no matter how small.
sentences.zh: 无论多么微小。

sentences.en: At one point, he declared about a particular design change,
sentences.zh: 有一次，针对某个特定的设计变更，他宣称：

sentences.en: I don't care what it costs.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎它花多少钱。

sentences.en: I don't care what scandal it causes.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎它会引起什么丑闻。

sentences.en: I don't care how long it takes.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎这需要多长时间。

sentences.en: That's what I want.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想要的。

sentences.en: That attitude explains why Utzon's Opera House is the most beautiful building in the world.
sentences.zh: 这种态度解释了为什么乌松的歌剧院是世界上最美丽的建筑。

sentences.en: It also made him the mother of all bottlenecks, especially as Utzon had a habit of disappearing for weeks at a time.
sentences.zh: 这也使他成为所有瓶颈的鼻祖，尤其是乌松有连续几周消失不见的习惯。

sentences.en: After his second visit to Sydney, Utzon decided to return to Denmark via China, Japan and Nepal.
sentences.zh: 在第二次访问悉尼后，乌松决定经由中国、日本和尼泊尔返回丹麦。

sentences.en: When he finally resurfaced, Arup jovially wrote,
sentences.zh: 当他终于重新露面时，阿鲁普诙谐地写道：

sentences.en: It was nice to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴听到你的消息。

sentences.en: I really thought you were lost in the wilds of Asia.
sentences.zh: 我真的以为你在亚洲的荒野中迷失了。

sentences.en: Utzon had hoped to pick up inspiration on his travels that he could use for the opera house, and he did.
sentences.zh: 乌松曾希望在旅行中汲取可用于歌剧院的灵感，他也确实做到了。

sentences.en: But decisions on the project ground to a halt without him.
sentences.zh: 但没有了他，项目的决策陷入了停顿。

sentences.en: And the problem of the roof was no joke.
sentences.zh: 而且屋顶的问题绝非小事。

sentences.en: Utzon's original magnificent doodle used a variety of different curves.
sentences.zh: 乌松最初宏伟的涂鸦运用了各种不同的曲线。

sentences.en: That caused two headaches.
sentences.zh: 这带来了两个头疼的问题。

sentences.en: The first was the expense.
sentences.zh: 首先是费用。

sentences.en: It made every section of the roof a unique construction.
sentences.zh: 这使得屋顶的每一个部分都成为独特的建筑。

sentences.en: The second was more serious.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题更为严重。

sentences.en: Arup had to spend a fortune on groundbreaking computer simulations
sentences.zh: 阿鲁普不得不花一大笔钱进行突破性的计算机模拟，

sentences.en: to figure out whether they would collapse under their own weight.
sentences.zh: 以弄清楚它们是否会在自身重量下坍塌。

sentences.en: Eventually, Arup concluded, that they would.
sentences.zh: 最终，阿鲁普得出结论：它们会的。

sentences.en: It was Utzon who solved the problem.
sentences.zh: 是乌松解决了这个问题。

sentences.en: In a flash of inspiration, he realised that each part of each vaulted roof,
sentences.zh: 灵光一闪间，他意识到拱形屋顶的每个部分，

sentences.en: large or small, could be proportioned as though it were sliced out of the same single enormous sphere.
sentences.zh: 无论大小，都可以按比例设计，就像是从同一个巨大的球体上切割下来的一样。

sentences.en: It doesn't sound like much, but the structural properties of these spherical curves were well understood.
sentences.zh: 这听起来没什么，但这些球形曲线的结构特性是人们十分了解的。

sentences.en: and, because the curves would all be identical, they could be built at much lower coSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，由于这些曲线将完全相同，它们的造价可以大大降低。

sentences.en: Utzon was delighted.
sentences.zh: 乌松很高兴。

sentences.en: It was the cheapest way of making it you could dream of.
sentences.zh: 这是你能梦想到的最便宜的建造方式。

sentences.en: All the work during these three years has been the background for arriving at this magnificent solution.
sentences.zh: 这三年来的所有工作都是为了得出这个宏伟解决方案的背景。

sentences.en: If they hadn't yet started construction, this would have been a triumphant moment.
sentences.zh: 如果他们还没有开始施工，这将是一个凯旋的时刻。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, construction had begun two and a half years earlier.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，施工已经在两年半前开始了。

sentences.en: The new design would require heavier supports than the ones they'd just built,
sentences.zh: 新设计将需要比他们刚建好的更重的支撑，

sentences.en: and the ones they'd just built were almost indestructible.
sentences.zh: 而他们刚建好的那些几乎是坚不可摧的。

sentences.en: The local contractor recommended dynamiting them, one by one, during the rush hour,
sentences.zh: 当地承包商建议在交通高峰期用炸药一个个炸掉它们，

sentences.en: so that the noise would be camouflaged by the traffic.
sentences.zh: 这样噪声就会被交通噪音掩盖。

sentences.en: That worked for a while, until a lump of concrete was blown high over the harbour and landed on a passing ferry.
sentences.zh: 这招起了一段时间作用，直到一块混凝土被炸飞到港口高空，落在一艘过往的渡轮上。

sentences.en: Another opera house bungle, yelled the local newspapers.
sentences.zh: “又一起歌剧院的 botched 工作（搞砸）”，当地报纸大喊。

sentences.en: Utzon had decided to move his office to Sydney to oversee proceedings.
sentences.zh: 乌松决定将办公室搬到悉尼来监督各项事宜。

sentences.en: That was a good idea, thought Arup's team, until Utzon told them he'd be travelling again.
sentences.zh: 在乌松告诉他们自己又要去旅行之前，阿鲁普的团队觉得这是个好主意，

sentences.en: and out of contact between Christmas and March.
sentences.zh: 并且在圣诞节到三月份期间将失联。

sentences.en: Arup begged him not to do this.
sentences.zh: 阿鲁普恳求他不要这样做。

sentences.en: There were so many decisions to be made
sentences.zh: 有那么多的决定需要做出，

sentences.en: and Utzon was the only person who could make them.
sentences.zh: 而乌松是唯一能做出这些决定的人。

sentences.en: But Utzon agreed only to a long meeting near London's Heathrow Airport
sentences.zh: 但乌松只同意在圣诞节后第二天

sentences.en: the day after Christmas to pin down a long list of details.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦希思罗机场附近开一个长会，以敲定长长的一份细节清单。

sentences.en: Utzon was persuaded to hurry the very last mile of his journey.
sentences.zh: 乌松被说服加快了他旅程的最后一程。

sentences.en: While flying from Tahiti to Sydney,
sentences.zh: 在从塔希提岛飞往悉尼的途中，

sentences.en: the DC-7 airliner's radio crackled into life with an invitation.
sentences.zh: DC-7客机的无线电突然传来了邀请。

sentences.en: Her Majesty the Queen was on the Royal Yacht in Sydney Harbour
sentences.zh: 英国女王陛下当时正在悉尼港的皇家游艇上，

sentences.en: and Mr Utzon was invited to lunch.
sentences.zh: 邀请乌松先生共进午餐。

sentences.en: After touchdown, he dashed to the Royal Reception.
sentences.zh: 着陆后，他冲向皇家招待会。

sentences.en: Arup's man on the ground wasn't impressed.
sentences.zh: 阿鲁普在现场的人一点也不觉得印象深刻。

sentences.en: Lo and behold, God appears from heaven.
sentences.zh: 看吧，上帝从天而降。

sentences.en: Utzon had descended from Tahiti, popped in for lunch with the Queen
sentences.zh: 乌重恩从塔希提岛归来，顺道与女王共进午餐

sentences.en: and then, grumbled the Arup engineer,
sentences.zh: 然后，奥鲁普的工程师抱怨道

sentences.en: In the afternoon he comes onto the site and starts complaining
sentences.zh: 下午他来到工地，开始抱怨

sentences.en: about some things he wasn't informed about.
sentences.zh: 一些他事先不知情的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, there was no-one we could contact.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根本没有人可以联系。

sentences.en: Four months later, July 1963,
sentences.zh: 四个月后的1963年7月，

sentences.en: the Opera House was scheduled to have been finished.
sentences.zh: 悉尼歌剧院原定于此时完工。

sentences.en: Yet the site on Bennelong Point
sentences.zh: 然而，贝尼朗岬的工地

sentences.en: was still just a huge, flat sprawl of concrete.
sentences.zh: 依然只是一片巨大而平坦的混凝土开阔地。

sentences.en: The basic outline of the broad, low podium was visible,
sentences.zh: 宽阔低矮的裙房基础轮廓依稀可见，

sentences.en: with the structure of the two sunken theatres scooped out of it.
sentences.zh: 其中两个下沉式剧场的结构已被挖掘出来。

sentences.en: There was no sign of walls, let alone the roof.
sentences.zh: 墙壁的影子都看不到，更不用说屋顶了。

sentences.en: In his history of the project, The Saga of Sydney Opera House,
sentences.zh: 建筑作家彼得·默里在其关于该项目的著作《悉尼歌剧院传奇》中，

sentences.en: architectural writer Peter Murray combs through the letters
sentences.zh: 梳理了奥韦·奥鲁普与约恩·乌重恩之间的书信，

sentences.en: between Uwe Arup and Jorn Utzon,
sentences.zh: 并发现这两个人的关系正在慢慢破裂。

sentences.en: and finds two men whose relationship is slowly falling apart.
sentences.zh: 乌重恩担心奥鲁普试图夺取控制权并抢占功劳。

sentences.en: Utzon worried that Arup was trying to take control and steal the credit.
sentences.zh: 奥鲁普则在寻退路。

sentences.en: Arup was eyeing the exits.
sentences.zh: 这是奥鲁普的话。

sentences.en: Here's Arup.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否考虑过找其他工程师来帮忙。

sentences.en: I do not know whether you have thought of getting other engineers to help you.
sentences.zh: 我很欢迎其他人来解决这些问题

sentences.en: I would welcome the idea of someone else solving the problems
sentences.zh: 并体验你的工作方法。

sentences.en: and experiencing your method of working.
sentences.zh: 乌重恩回应道，

sentences.en: Utzon responded,
sentences.zh: 亲爱的奥韦，请停止你的批评。

sentences.en: Dear Uwe, please desist from your criticism.
sentences.zh: 管理在某种程度上是工作中最简单的一部分，

sentences.en: Management is in a way the easiest part of the job,
sentences.zh: 这是大多数人都能学会的。

sentences.en: something which most people can learn.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许吧。

sentences.en: Well, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 没有人怀疑乌重恩作为建筑师的天赋。

sentences.zh: 有人告诉乌松，因为他已经辞职，他将再也无法在丹麦接手任何政府项目。

sentences.en: He taught for a while in Hawaii and anonymously designed some buildings for a friend's architecture practice.
sentences.zh: 他在夏威夷教过一段时间书，并匿名替朋友的建筑事务所设计了一些建筑。

sentences.en: He did win a commission to design something big in Kuwait, but Saddam Hussein's army set fire to that in 1991.
sentences.zh: 他确实赢得了一项在科威特设计大型建筑的委托，但在1991年被萨达姆·侯赛因的军队付之一炬。

sentences.en: In a Copenhagen suburb, he built a humble church.
sentences.zh: 在哥本哈根的一个郊区，他建造了一座简朴的教堂。

sentences.en: It's unprepossessing on the outside,
sentences.zh: 它从外面看起来并不起眼，

sentences.en: but on the inside there's a gorgeous ceiling that looks like folds of cloth
sentences.zh: 但内部却有一个华丽的天花板，看起来像层层叠叠的布匹

sentences.en: parting to reveal the light of heaven.
sentences.zh: 向两旁分开，透出天堂的光芒。

sentences.en: Apparently, it had something similar in mind for the interior of the opera house.
sentences.zh: 显然，他为歌剧院内部的设计也抱有类似的想法。

sentences.en: But nobody wanted to give him another chance to display his genius on the stage it deserved.
sentences.zh: 但没有人愿意再给他一次机会，在应得的舞台上展现他的天才。

sentences.en: The price of the Sydney Opera House?
sentences.zh: 悉尼歌剧院的代价是什么？

sentences.en: It was all those other buildings that Jorn Utzon was never allowed to design.
sentences.zh: 那就是约恩·乌松再也没有机会设计的那些建筑。

sentences.en: Eventually, the architecture profession woke up and began showering prizes on him,
sentences.zh: 最终，建筑界醒悟过来，开始向他颁发各种奖项，

sentences.en: often acknowledging, regretfully, that Utzon hadn't built much besides the opera house.
sentences.zh: 人们常常带着遗憾承认，乌松除了歌剧院之外并没有建造太多作品。

sentences.en: But it was too late to change that.
sentences.zh: 但要改变这一点已经太迟了。

sentences.en: When he won architecture's Nobel Prize, the Pritzker, he was 85 years old.
sentences.zh: 当他获得建筑界的最高荣誉普利兹克奖时，他已经85岁高龄了。

sentences.en: The opera house itself had started to become embarrassed by the controversy
sentences.zh: 歌剧院本身也开始对当年的争议感到尴尬，

sentences.en: and that graceless plaque that didn't even mention Utzon's name.
sentences.zh: 还有那块甚至没有提及乌松名字的不光彩饰板。

sentences.en: In the 1990s, they attempted a rapprochement,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代，他们试图修复关系，

sentences.en: naming a room in his honour and asking him to help design a new wing.
sentences.zh: 以他的名字命名了一个房间，并邀请他协助设计新翼楼。

sentences.en: Still, he didn't come.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他还是没有去。

sentences.en: He sent his son to give a speech, explaining that his elderly father
sentences.zh: 他派儿子去发表了一篇演讲，解释说他年迈的父亲

sentences.en: lives and breathes the Opera House, and as its creator, he just has to close his eyes to see it.
sentences.zh: 对歌剧院魂牵梦绕，作为它的创造者，他只需闭上眼睛就能看见它。

sentences.en: One person who sneered at the peacemaking was Davis Hughes, an old man like Utzon himself.
sentences.zh: 有一个对这种化干戈为玉帛的做法嗤之以鼻的人，那就是戴维斯·休斯，他和乌松一样是个老人。

sentences.en: He phoned the chairman of the Opera House management team
sentences.zh: 他给歌剧院管理团队的主席打了电话，

sentences.en: and ranted for 45 minutes about the very idea of asking Utzon his opinion on anything.
sentences.zh: 长篇大论地抱怨了45分钟，反对征求乌松对任何事情的意见。

sentences.en: I did Utzon a favour, he said.
sentences.zh: 我是在帮乌松的忙，他说。

sentences.en: I put him out of his misery like you put down a dog.
sentences.zh: 我结束了他的痛苦，就像对一条快不行的狗施行安乐死一样。

sentences.en: Late in Utzon's life, a British architect named John Pardy
sentences.zh: 在乌松晚年的时候，一位名叫约翰·帕迪的英国建筑师

sentences.en: went to visit him in Mallorca, where he'd spent most of his later years.
sentences.zh: 去马略卡岛探望了他，他晚年的大部分时光都是在那里度过的。

sentences.en: It was a kind of pilgrimage to meet one of the true greats of architecture.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是拜访建筑界真正巨匠的一次朝圣之旅。

sentences.en: Utzon had designed the home, of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，这座住宅是乌松自己设计的，

sentences.en: and Pardee described its
sentences.zh: 帕迪形容它有一种

sentences.en: glare-free hush that seemed to transport me to another world.
sentences.zh: 无眩光的宁静，仿佛能把我带到另一个世界。

sentences.en: They talked about this and that.
sentences.zh: 他们东拉西扯地聊了聊。

sentences.en: The old man expressed the occasional pain at the Opera House affair,
sentences.zh: 这位老人对歌剧院事件偶尔流露出痛苦，

sentences.en: but this was all a long time ago, he said.
sentences.zh: 但他说，这一切都是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Utzon had never been back to Sydney.
sentences.zh: 乌松从未回过悉尼。

sentences.en: He'd designed the most beautiful building of the 20th century
sentences.zh: 他设计了20世纪最美丽的建筑，

sentences.en: and he'd never seen it.
sentences.zh: 却从未亲眼见过它。

sentences.en: Sensing that Utzon had left some part of his heart in Sydney,
sentences.zh: 察觉到乌松将部分心血留在了悉尼，

sentences.en: Pardy offered to help the old man travel back.
sentences.zh: 帕迪提出要帮助这位老人重返故地。

sentences.en: Utzon's wife pulled Pardy aside.
sentences.zh: 乌松的妻子把帕迪拉到一旁。

sentences.en: That wasn't possible, she said.
sentences.zh: 这不可能，她说。

sentences.en: It would kill him.
sentences.zh: 那会要了他的命。

sentences.en: Did she mean the arduous journey?
sentences.zh: 她是说旅途的艰辛吗？

sentences.en: Or did she mean the memories?
sentences.zh: 还是指那些回忆？
